newsitem.title: USA: Online ad revenues hit record $129.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Online ad revenues hit record $129.5 million.

text.p: Online advertising revenues jumped 18 percent to $129.5 million in the first quarter from record fourth quarter levels, the Internet Advertising Bureau said Thursday.

Total ad spending in the first quarter rose 333 percent from year-ago levels of just under $30 million, the bureau said. The IAB's survey found that online ad revenue is being spread more evenly across the largest online publishers.
For example, in the first quarter the top 10 publishers online accounted for 63 percent of advertising revenues, compared with 75 percent one year ago.

"Media spending is traditionally soft in the first quarter, so these are particularly significant results," said Rich LeFurgy, IAB chairman and an official at ESPN/ABC Internet Ventures. "Acceptance of the medium is clearly growing among advertisers and more and more publishers now view advertising as the revenue model of choice."

The survey represents data from more than 200 Internet publishers representing more than 86 percent of industry revenues. It reported that 45 percent of respondents forecast 1997 revenues to total between $500 million and $600 million, while 17 percent forecast revenues of more than $700 million.

Online advertising revenues for 1996 were $267 million, with $109.5 million recorded in the fourth quarter, according to the IAB, whose "Advertising Revenue Reporting Program" is compiled by Coopers & Lybrand LLP's New Media Group.

Five leading industry categories dominated Internet advertising spending in the first quarter. Computing products accounted for 30 percent, telecommunications for 22 percent, consumer-related businesses for 17 percent, financial services for 11 percent and new media businesses for 10 percent.
